title: IDF Confirms Killing of Two Hamas Commanders — Oct. 7 Hostage-Holder Mushtaha and Khan Younis Cmdr Qawari
detail: The IDF announced on August 14, 2026 that it had killed Hudhaifa Khaled Suleiman Qawari, a company commander in Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade, in an aerial strike in the southern Gaza Strip. The military said Qawari had been involved in training Hamas fighters, transporting weapons, and working to rebuild the group's capabilities, and that he "recently advanced terror attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians," justifying the strike as self-defense during the ceasefire under provisions permitting Israeli operations against imminent threats. Precise munitions and aerial surveillance were used to reduce civilian harm, the IDF said. Separately, the military also confirmed it had killed Muhammad Bassam Mushtaha, a commander in Hamas's Al-Shati battalion, in a northern Gaza airstrike on July 30, 2026 — only revealing the strike two weeks later. Mushtaha had held custody of multiple Israelis kidnapped on October 7, 2023, including Tsachi Idan and Cpl. Noa Marciano (both killed in captivity) and Ziv Berman, Omri Miran, Ori Megidish, Naama Levy, and Matan Angrest (all later freed or rescued). The dual announcements are part of what the Times of Israel described as an escalating Israeli campaign of retribution strikes targeting every participant in the October 7 attack.

media.caption: IDF confirms killing of Hamas Khan Younis Brigade company commander Hudhaifa Qawari in a southern Gaza strike

title: Kushner, Mladenov and Blair to Visit Israel and Egypt for Gaza Talks After Netanyahu's Plan Rejection
detail: Board of Peace envoys announced August 14, 2026 that Jared Kushner, Director General Nickolay Mladenov, and executive board member Tony Blair will travel to Israel and then Cairo the following week to press forward on the US-backed Gaza roadmap, after Prime Minister Netanyahu's August 9 rejection of the plan's disarmament-for-withdrawal terms. A Board of Peace official said the delegation will "hear the concerns that have been raised and talk about next steps." In Israel, the group is expected to meet Netanyahu and senior officials to address opposition to provisions requiring simultaneous Hamas disarmament and IDF withdrawal; in Cairo they will meet Egyptian, Qatari, and Turkish mediators working with the Palestinian technocratic committee slated to administer Gaza. The trip comes amid continued reports of ceasefire violations, with at least 1,260 Palestinians killed and 4,150+ wounded since the October 2025 truce took effect, and a surge in settler violence in the West Bank.

media.caption: Kushner, Mladenov, and Blair to travel to Israel and Egypt to press the stalled Gaza peace roadmap
